# dsh-chrome-attach
**Attach the current Chrome tab to your conversation.** One pick in the composer screenshots the pag
e you are looking at, drops it into the draft as an image attachment, and types the tab's **title an
d URL** on a line next to it — the same move as ChatGPT's *+ → attach browser page*, except the mode
l also learns *which* page it is looking at. Everything waits in the draft; nothing is sent until yo
*which* page it is looking at. Everything waits in the draft; nothing is sent until you press Enter.
简体中文 · a DeepSeek Harness plugin
The plugin tries three capture tiers in order and uses the first one that works. **No bridge, no ext
ension and no Chrome flags are required** — only the image quality differs:
| Tier | What the image contains | Needs | Notes |
| `bridge` | tab content only | `dsh-chrome-bridge` + the DSH Bridge extension | best: no focus stea

ling, no prompt, supports full-page |
| `cdp` | tab content only | Chrome's own **Remote debugging**

switch | one approval, keeps your normal profile |
| `window` | the whole Chrome window (**includin
g** tab strip and address bar) | macOS + Screen Recording permission | no extension; isolates Chrome
without changing focus |
The default chain is `bridge → cdp → window`; the first tier that succeeds wins. Every response name
s its `source`, and a window shot is labelled *"window shot, browser UI included"*.

es the page line). On older builds the screenshot still attaches; only the line is skipped, and the

## Use
The `+` menu in the composer gains one row, right below *Add files* in the Add section:
> **[Chrome mark] Attach Chrome** · *Screenshot the page, plus its title and URL*
Clicking it screenshots the active tab (or degrades to the window), puts the image into the current
draft, writes the page line, and **does not send**. Keep typing. `/attach` works too.
An image only tells the model what the pixels look like, not which page it came from, so the row als
o inserts one line through the composer's own input facade:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
That line and the image are one draft: it is plain text you can edit or delete, and both leave toget
her when you press Enter. If the draft is mid-send or no editable draft is attached, only the image
lands and the toast says the page line was skipped (`已附上（页面地址未能写入输入框）：…`).
Attachment names carry the page title, e.g. `DeepSeek-Harness-155812.png`.
Full-page capture exists in the API (`POST /api/chrome-attach/shot {"full":true}`) but is not a sepa
exists in the API (`POST /api/chrome-attach/shot {"full":true}`) but is not a separate menu row yet.
## Capture setups
### 1. `bridge` — no permissions at all
Install `dsh-chrome-bridge` from the DSH plugin page and the **DSH Bridge** extension in Chrome, the
n connect once. The plugin shells out to the `cb` CLI (`~/.dsh/bin/cb`) and gets the bare tab conten
t, without stealing focus.
### 2. `cdp` — Chrome's own Remote debugging switch
The clean-tab fallback that needs no extension and no Screen Recording. Chrome 136 changed `--remote
-debugging-port`, but Chrome now ships a supported switch instead:

1. Open `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` and tick **Remote debugging**.
2. Click **Attach Chrome

** in DSH; the first connection asks once whether to allow the app — allow it.
3. Chrome writes the
chosen port to `<profile>/DevToolsActivePort`, and the plugin reads it. Your profile, logins and ext
ensions stay exactly as they are.
The switch is governed by the `DevToolsRemoteDebuggingAllowed` policy. On a managed machine where it
is disabled the checkbox is greyed out — use the `window` tier or `bridge` instead.
Already launching Chrome with a debug port? The plugin also probes `9222`/`9223` and any port named
by `DSH_CHROME_DEBUG_PORT`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The host half only imports Node built-ins, so it never depends on packages the DSH profile may not r
esolve. The client half is the entry in the `+` menu; it hands the PNG to the same attachment intake
a real drag-and-drop uses. The page line goes through `inputActions`, the façade the conversation p
ublishes to session slots as a prop — the plugin registers one headless `conversation.input.dock` en
try to hold on to it, so it never reaches into the session directly and inherits the façade's phase/
o it, so it never reaches into the session directly and inherits the façade's phase/revision guards.
## Limitations

- Captures only the **active tab** (`bridge`/`cdp`) or the **frontmost Chrome window** (`window`).
-
The page line is typed into the focused draft, so it needs an editable composer; while a message is

being sent the image attaches but the line is skipped (the toast says so).
- A `window` shot's URL/

title come from the same page, so they describe the frontmost tab rather than the whole window.
- `c
hrome://` pages and the Chrome Web Store cannot be captured through `chrome.debugger`; the `window`

tier is unaffected.
- The `window` tier needs Screen Recording; failures point at the exact System S

ettings pane.
